payload.name: Store Explicit Counts for Enumerated Sets
payload.description: When constructing memories from a message that introduces or names a new member of a countable set (e.g., pets, children, vehicles) and the full set is explicitly enumerated in the conversation, include the explicit total count in the extracted candidate or memory update.
content: During extraction, when a message names a new member of a countable set (pets, children, vehicles, etc.) and the conversation explicitly enumerates all current members, include the explicit total count in the candidate content, not just the individual member.

During CRUD, when ADDing or UPDATEing a memory that describes a set of named items, ensure the stored content contains the explicit aggregate count if the source conversation supports it; do not rely on the reader to count separate memories.

solves: Future questions asking 'how many' of a person's countable possessions (pets, children, vehicles) fail when memory contains individual named entries but no explicit total. The diagnosed cause is extraction recording each new member without synthesizing the aggregate count, even when the conversation enumerates the complete set. The reusable rule is to store the explicit total whenever all members are named in the source; it does not apply when the set is only partially mentioned or the count must be guessed.
